t: From about 1220 to the 1440s the lords of northern Yucatán shared power in the walled city of Mayapan under the leadership of the Cocom.
Its potters made god-shaped incense burners, and its canoe traders linked Yucatán with the Gulf Coast, Belize and Honduras.
Around 1441 a Xiu-led revolt killed the Cocom lords; Mayapan was abandoned and Yucatán split into rival provinces.
dyk: According to Diego de Landa, one son of the Cocom ruler survived the massacre of his family at Mayapan only because he was away trading in Honduras.
ev: Chichen Itza loses its dominance over northern Yucatán
Chronicles place Hunac Ceel's overthrow of Chac Xib Chac of Chichen Itza in this katun
Mayapan emerges as the capital of a confederacy of northern Yucatec lords
Mass graves of dismembered, burned bodies mark violence inside the city
A long drought begins as rivalry grows between the Cocom and the Xiu
Nobles led by the Xiu kill the Cocom ruler; Mayapan is sacked and abandoned
The Cocom of Sotuta massacre Xiu pilgrims at Otzmal
The Spanish found Mérida, and the Xiu lord of Maní makes peace with them

f.founder: Hunac Ceel (according to colonial Maya chronicles)
f.successor: Some sixteen provinces, including Maní, Sotuta and Ah Kin Chel
